sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Hittites
sources.note: Direct essay read, paragraphs 1-3, Suppiluliuma expansion, concluding successor paragraph. Broad chronology adopted; older exact reign dates and assertion Hattusha violently destroyed before abandonment are not used. Modern abandonment evidence comes from Manning et al.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Hattusha, the Hittite Capital
sources.note: Direct Brief synthesis and Authenticity sections: walls over 8 km, upper double wall with over 100 towers, gates/tunnel, Great Temple, Yazilikaya, granaries and ponds.

sources.title: Türkiye Memory of the World nomination: Hittite cuneiform tablets from Boğazköy
sources.note: Direct PDF, printed page 1 archive contents; page 3 queen and seal; page 14 figure 12 Qadesh treaty; page 22 figure 25 Akkadian letter from Naptera to Puduhepa. Outdated exclusive-source and first-ever-treaty claims deliberately not adopted.

sources.title: Jürgen Seeher: Water supply and water use in the Lower City of Hattusha
sources.note: Direct German abstract. Istanbuler Mitteilungen 60 (2010), pp. 67-80; repository publication date 2024 is digitization, not excavation date. Coring in 2002 supported probable reservoir in depression behind earth banks; no household piped-water or toilet claim.

sources.title: University of Texas Linguistics Research Center: The Law Code, Old Hittite
sources.note: Direct lesson, transcriptions and translations of clauses 10, 28, 66 and 86. These are prescriptions, not measured compliance. Clause 2 translation has a numerical mismatch with transcription; it is not used.

sources.title: Theo P. J. van den Hout: Educational Principles in the Hittite Empire
sources.note: Direct University of Chicago scholarly lecture, paragraphs on family crafts, training fee, Reading and writing, scribal family tree. Avoided outdated horse-riding claim, experimental stable health inference and value comparisons.

sources.title: Peter Raulwing: The Kikkuli Text, Hittite Training Instructions for Chariot Horses
sources.note: Direct author scholarly study, 2009; printed pp. 3-5: training, feeding/rest/care, archive of building E, four tablets and copying chronology. Do not equate every Hittite horse text with Kikkuli or promise modern training efficacy.

sources.title: Giulia Torri, Scuola Normale Superiore Mnamon: Cuneiform Hittite
sources.note: Direct Introduction and Graphic system, revised 2022. Adaptation of Akkadian cuneiform, languages and logograms. Distinct from the companion Hittite language article; latter not needed for this card.

sources.title: University of Texas Linguistics Research Center: The Plague Prayer of Mursilis II
sources.note: Direct lesson by Sara E. Kimball, Winfred P. Lehmann and Jonathan Slocum. First paragraph based on KUB XIV 10 + KUB XXVI 86; exact segmented transcription ki-i-ma ku-it i-ya-at-ten and Translation paragraph 1. Exact English: What is this that you have done? Source attributes twenty years of deaths to the king; no modern disease diagnosis inferred.

sources.title: Manning, Kocik, Lorentzen and Sparks: Severe multi-year drought coincident with Hittite collapse
sources.note: Nature 614 (2023), 719-724. Direct open redirected to blocked identity service; indexed primary full article retrieved by query site:nature.com "s41586-022-05693-y" "1198". Read abandonment paragraph, tree-ring results, and historical chronology section. Around 1198-1196 BCE is approximate, dating uncertainty discussed; drought is contributory hypothesis, not demonstrated sole cause.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Silver vessel terminating in a stag
sources.note: Direct catalogue, object 1989.281.10, fourteenth-thirteenth century BCE, silver/gold inlay. Construction and frieze description used; older historical introduction dates not adopted. Intended ritual use is an interpretation, not certainty.

proposedOverrides.name: Hittite Kingdom and Empire
proposedOverrides.summary: An Anatolian kingdom and empire centered on Hattusha, with cuneiform archives and extensive international diplomacy.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Existing indexed Hittites record; rename display to Hittite Kingdom and Empire. No new identities or geometry. Narrative distinguishes kingdom/empire from earlier Anatolia and later successor states.
batchIdentityNotes.publicCaveat: The opening explicitly warns that map coverage begins before the kingdom and repeats a large outline centuries after imperial collapse. Periods and ending distinguish later successor traditions.
